title: Language changes and pronunciation support
learningObjectives: Explain language changes and pronunciation support and apply inclusive web accessibility practices.

understand.concept: The lang attribute can identify language changes within a document. Marking a phrase or passage with its correct language helps assistive technologies choose pronunciation rules and supports text processing. Direction may also need to be declared separately using dir.
understand.whyItMatters: Without language metadata, screen readers may pronounce words using the wrong language rules. Multilingual pages should mark passages accurately rather than relying only on visual styling.
understand.analogy: lang is like a pronunciation note attached to a passage so reading tools know which language rules to use.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; accessible names, language, and interaction behaviour must follow platform accessibility rules.

explain.narrative: Each passage declares its language; the Arabic example also declares right-to-left direction.

practise.guidedTask: Create a paragraph that switches between English, Telugu, and another language. Mark each language and explain the effect on pronunciation tools.
practise.independentTask: Perform an accessibility review of a small page. Test keyboard-only use, labels, language metadata, media alternatives, and assistive technology output where available.
hints: Keep ARIA states synchronized with real interface state.
Provide text alternatives for meaningful non-text content.

questions.prompt: Which attribute marks the language of a passage?
questions.explanation: lang identifies the language of the text in that element.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest baseline for accessible HTML?
options: Semantic native HTML, clear labels, keyboard support, and testing
questions.answer: Semantic native HTML, clear labels, keyboard support, and testing
questions.explanation: Accessibility starts with semantic structure and working interactions, then uses ARIA only where needed.
